policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV uses plural agreement for the subject ('My people have been lost sheep' and 'they have gone'), distinguishing qere plural hayu from ketiv singular hayah.
ASV renders an active verb with a pronominal object, 'they have turned them away,' distinguishing qere shovavum from ketiv shovavim.
ASV has the plural imperative 'Flee out ... and go forth,' distinguishing qere tse'u from ketiv yets'u.

ASV addresses a plural group with 'ye are glad,' distinguishing the qere plural verb from the ketiv feminine singular form; the alternative-rendering note concerns different English wording and does not decide this unit.

ASV addresses a plural group with 'ye rejoice,' distinguishing the qere plural verb from the ketiv feminine singular form; the alternative-rendering note concerns different English wording and does not decide this unit.

ASV addresses a plural group with 'ye are wanton,' distinguishing the qere plural verb from the ketiv feminine singular form; the alternative-rendering note concerns different English wording and does not decide this unit.

ASV continues the plural address with 'neigh as strong horses,' distinguishing the qere plural verb from the ketiv feminine singular form; the alternative-rendering note concerns different English wording and does not decide this unit.
ASV 'her bulwarks are fallen' does not distinguish the qere and ketiv spellings, and the Hebrew-gloss note ('given her hand') concerns another expression in the verse.

ASV explicitly supplies the pronominal object in 'recompense her according to her work,' distinguishing qere lah from the ketiv omission; the alternative-rendering note does not decide a textual reading.
ASV's causative wording 'I will suddenly make them run away' distinguishes qere aritsem from ketiv arutsem.
